content.jointProblem: What combination of weld condition, service loading, temperature variation and moisture explains cracking in AutomVoj’s painted mild-steel conveyor joints, and which feasible manufacturing or design changes could reduce it? The first experiment would compare representative production-welded joints under field-informed cyclic loading at room temperature and 2–6 °C, with controlled moisture conditions, to test whether the published thermo-mechanical fatigue methods transfer to this application.

rationale.text: Erić has directly investigated interacting thermal and mechanical fatigue in welded structural steel, providing a relevant experimental foundation for testing AutomVoj’s suspected combined-loading mechanism.

sources.quote: superimposed thermal cycling (between −30 °C and +20 °C at 0.5 cycles per hour) during mechanical fatigue loading

rationale.text: His field assessment work connects measured operational stress spectra with simultaneous temperature records, supporting a service-informed test programme rather than an arbitrary laboratory load.

sources.quote: Rainflow-counted stress spectra and simultaneous temperature records were used to construct a combined loading environment for assessment.

rationale.text: He has measured weld residual stresses and compared them with thermal–mechanical simulations, which is relevant to investigating welding-process contributions to cracking.

sources.quote: Residual stresses in as-welded and post-weld heat-treated (PWHT) T-joint specimens of S460M low-alloy steel were measured by hole-drilling with strain-gauge rosettes
compared with sequentially coupled thermal–mechanical FE simulations.

rationale.text: His group routinely uses fatigue-testing equipment, a climate chamber and fracture-mechanics models, offering a relevant starting point for addressing the company’s testing gap.

sources.quote: The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C,
in-house FE models built in Abaqus for residual-stress and fracture-mechanics analyses.

constraints.text: Tests and models must represent painted mild-steel hollow sections and the actual crossmember-to-stringer connection; results from different steels or specimen geometries cannot substitute for application-specific validation.

sources.quote: Our conveyor frames are welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery.
weld joint cracking at the main crossmember-to-stringer connections

constraints.text: The experimental environment must represent 2–6 °C service and establish the actual thermal, moisture and vibration histories; these suspected contributors must be tested rather than assumed causal.

sources.quote: Our suspicion is that the combination of thermal cycling, condensation, and the vibration load from loaded belts

constraints.text: Failure analysis must make deliberate use of the existing site evidence and two retained failed sections; destructive examination needs an agreed sampling plan.

sources.quote: We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage.

constraints.text: Combined cold and cyclic-load testing requires external laboratory provision and advance equipment scheduling; the researcher’s chamber and fatigue machine are shared resources.

sources.quote: We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load.
Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

constraints.text: The company must reserve engineering time for evidence collection, specimen production and review because development personnel also support live projects.

sources.quote: We have no dedicated R&D department
our chief engineer and two senior automation engineers who allocate time between live projects and improvement work.

risks: Transfer is unproven: the cited studies largely concern specified structural steels, different weld geometries and colder or wider thermal cycles than this 2–6 °C application. The first comparative experiment must test applicability before using their models for conveyor-life predictions.

Condensation-driven corrosion or coating damage could dominate or interact with fatigue, but the supplied material does not demonstrate validated corrosion-fatigue methods for painted conveyor sections. Additional expertise or facilities may be needed.
Two failed sections may not capture variability across the 14 replaced assemblies, and missing service histories could prevent a unique root-cause conclusion.
Accelerated laboratory tests may change the damage mechanism and cannot by themselves establish performance over 18 months of service.
Researcher availability is unknown, and shared equipment may delay extended campaigns. Humidity-control capability and specimen-size compatibility are not established.
Budget, delivery deadline, customer-site access and available company engineering time are unknown; any could limit the investigation or validation scope.
questions: What is Erić’s availability, who would perform the experimental work, and when can the shared chamber and fatigue machine be reserved?
Can the laboratory control and measure condensation or humidity at 2–6 °C while applying representative cyclic loads, and can it accommodate the actual connection geometry?
Can AutomVoj provide steel grades, wall thicknesses, drawings, welding procedures, filler specifications, inspection records, coating details and traceability for failed and unaffected frames?
Can the two retained sections be examined before destructive sampling, and are additional failed sections or matched unfailed production joints available?
Can customer sites be instrumented to obtain load and strain spectra, temperature and humidity histories, operating cycles, and relevant washdown or maintenance conditions?
What budget, deadline and engineering time can AutomVoj commit, and what evidence would it require before implementing a welding, filler or joint-design change?

How will the partners agree the initial comparison, replication and mechanism checks, and subsequently validate any proposed mitigation without assuming accelerated tests reproduce 18-month service life?
